---
title: "Pipeline"
---

Scripts are numbered in the order they run. Each one writes to
`<DATA_ROOT>/data/outputs/` and reads what the previous step wrote. Run them from the
repository root:

```bash
uv run python scripts/20_subsets/21_prepare_input_data.py
```

Most steps take minutes. The two model scripts take hours over the full site list.

## 10_datasets: assemble the site collection

| Script | What it does | Writes |
|--------|--------------|--------|
| `00_find_overlaps.py` | Lists sites present in both AmeriFlux and FLUXNET-SHUTTLE | `10_datasets/` |
| `11_collect_info.py` | Scans all five raw sources, one row per dataset found | `11_datasets_info.csv` |
| `12_create_parquet.py` | Merges the datasets of a site into one parquet file, resolving frequency and overlapping years by source priority | `12_parquet_merged/`, `12_datasets_info_parquet.csv` |
| `13_check_available_vars.py` | Records which of NEE, LE, GPP, RECO, TA, VPD, SWIN, SWC exist per site and under which column name | `13_datasets_info_parquet_vars.csv` |
| `13b_check_available_vars_SWC.py` | Same for the soil moisture depth variants | `13b_variables_coverage_summary.csv` |
| `14_collect_basic_stats.py` | Record counts, date ranges, min/max/mean per variable | `14_datasets_info_parquet_vars_stats.csv` |
| `15_remove_sites.py` | Applies the inclusion criteria and drops the rest | `15_datasets_info_parquet_vars_stats_usedsites.csv` |
| `16a` + `16b` | ERA5 1991-2020 normals from Google Earth Engine, run in parallel batches | `16_ERA5_climate_1991-2020_GoogleEarthEngine/` |
| `16c` + `16d` | Same from the Copernicus CDS API | `16_ERA5_climate_1991-2020_Copernicus/` |
| `16_download_era5_mat_map.py` | CDS download for the older FLUXNET2015 sites, which carry no 1991-2020 ERA5 in their own files | `16_ERA5_climate_1991-2020/` |
| `17_add_era5_info.py` | Picks one ERA5 source per site and adds MAT and MAP | `17_datasets_info_parquet_vars_stats_usedsites_era5.csv` |

The `16*` scripts need credentials and can be skipped if the ERA5 output folders are
already populated. Script `17` writes a timestamped log with the full decision trail
for every site.

## 20_subsets: build the model input

`21_prepare_input_data.py` turns each merged site parquet into the subset the models
see. Per site:

1. keep the four months with the highest mean GPP
2. keep measured NEE only, quality flag 0, no gap-filled fluxes
3. keep daytime records, `SW_IN_POT > 20`
4. balance the record so every one of the four months contributes the same number of
   years, dropping the oldest years where needed
5. drop records with any missing predictor
6. derive ET from LE and TA, and NEP as `-NEE`
7. z-score every variable within the site and keep both the measured and the z-scored
   columns

Writes one parquet per site to `20_subsets/21_subsets_parquet/`, a heatmap per site,
and the summary table `21_SUBSETS_parquet_vars_stats_subsets.csv`.

::: {.callout-note}
One site, CD-Ygb, has VPD in the wrong units in the source files. The correction is
applied in this script.
:::

## 30_shap: fit models and explain them

`31_shap.py` trains the models and calculates SHAP values. It has two modes, switched
at the top of the file:

```python
TUNE_HYPERPARAMETERS = False   # SHAP analysis (default)
TUNE_HYPERPARAMETERS = True    # hyperparameter search instead
TUNE_N_ITER = 25               # combinations tested per site in tuning mode
```

In SHAP mode each site gets 5-fold cross-validation. Within each fold the 80 % training
part is split again into 68 % for fitting and 12 % for early stopping, and the held-out
20 % is explained. Every observation therefore receives SHAP values from a model that
never saw it. Per-fold R² and RMSE go to the log, and the folds are reassembled in the
original index order.

Writes per-site parquet and CSV with features, SHAP values and predictions, plus one
aggregated CSV holding the fold metrics for all sites.

`32_validate_shap_methods.py` fits one model per site on an 85/15 split and calculates
ALE curves on 100 grid points per feature. ALE is a second read on the same fitted
models: it shows the isolated effect of a feature on the prediction, where SHAP
attributes each individual prediction. Writes `{SITE}_ale_curves_{TARGET}.csv` per site,
which is what the aggregation and figure scripts consume.

## 40_aggregation: combine site results

| Script | What it does |
|--------|--------------|
| `41_binagg_per_site.py` | Bins each site's SHAP values on a two-variable grid, using fixed custom bin edges so all sites share one grid |
| `42_binagg_across_sites.py` | Averages the binned grids across all sites, one vote per site |
| `43_binagg_across_igbp.py` | Same, separately per IGBP forest type |
| `44_agg_per_scenario.py` | Averages SHAP values within the nine stress stages, per site and then across sites |

Equal weighting throughout: a site with 20 years of data counts the same as a site with
three. Bins that fewer than half of the sites reach are dropped from the aggregated
grids.
